title: How design thinking can reach product development breakthroughs with agile
excerpt: We are living in a highly connected and demanding world, where customers know what they want. Everything from doctors’ appointment to ordering groceries is a few mobile taps away
author: PM Admin

children.text: We are living in a highly connected and demanding world, where customers know what they want. Everything from doctors’ appointments to ordering groceries is a few mobile taps away. Organizations are striving to deliver personalized experiences to their customers for better retention by being available in real-time on any device and at any location. The products and services developed and delivered to the customers are intended to provide a unique and memorable user experience.

Most projects are generated from an idea and get developed into a product. Fully tech-driven products fail to satisfy the end-user or do not leave the impact as expected. The reason is that the idea that led to the product development did not resonate with the customer’s requirement.

With design thinking and Agile duo, the customer perspective is given the utmost importance considering the product is being developed for the consumer. The question is how design thinking can be applied to agile software development and how will that help.
What is Design Thinking?

Design thinking is a method for practical and creative problem-solving. It is an approach to designing a solution for a problem from the customer’s point of view. Instead of getting the product ready and then asking the customers to use it, design thinking enables a product to be developed based on customers’ needs.

Here, we ask the customers what they want and then find possible solutions to answer the pain point. Before the product is developed, customers are asked to evaluate the prototype and share their feedback. With multiple solutions and prototypes, we reduce the risk of failure of the main product and instead go through a few prototype failures.
There are various stages of Design Thinking:
Empathize:

In this stage, we ask our customers’ needs and pain points. We collect this data from random people using feedback, interviews, questionnaire surveys, etc. Understanding user feelings and their way of thinking helps us look at the problem with a fresh outlook. Most people think they know what their customers want. The best way to be sure is to ask the customer and collect as much data as you can. Do not remove the filters, do not manipulate or edit the data, it is purely a collection phase.
‘Depending on assumption is the shortest way to failure’
Define:

We analyze the data collected and understand our target audience. The target audience may fall under different categories based on their age, gender, job type, location, religion, ethnicity, etc. So, if you have more than one category of customers, then bucket them under different names. Based on these identifications, we create customer personas. Each persona problem may differ slightly and so will their solution. In this stage, we define the problem as best as we can.
Ideate:

Here is when your team brainstorms with each other, works individually, uses sticky notes, or jot down in a notepad or whiteboard. The team comes up with ideas for solutions that solve the problem defined in the previous stage. There may be some 10 to 50 ideas and out of these bundle of ideas, we select the 2 or 3 best fitting solutions.
Prototype:

Before diving into the complete software development process for 3 different ideas, we create a prototype for ideas. These prototypes are the actual physical form of the solution and are highly interactive. These are not presentations or online demos but interactive functional forms that can be given to the customers to use. It’s a cheap substitute for the main product, takes less time and if there are any problems, we can fix them in the prototype itself.
Test:

Evaluate the performance of your prototype by recording user experience. Make sure that you don’t give your users a user guide to use the prototype, or else the whole purpose is lost. We want to test if the prototype is the most obvious solution to the problem.

title: Next.js vs. Nuxt.js vs. Nest.js: Choosing the Right Framework for Your Needs

author: PM Admin

children.text: Developing an application requires a strong core that largely depends on the chosen technology stack. A robust technology stack ensures the application is efficient, scalable, secure, and built for long-term success. The overall project performance depends on this choice.

One of the key considerations after choosing the technology stack is the programming language framework used. If JavaScript is part of your tech stack, it’s crucial to explore frameworks that can streamline and improve your development process.

JavaScript frameworks are collections of pre-written JS code libraries that help develop web applications by streamlining the process, enabling developers to focus on writing the unique parts of their application. Among the popular options,
Next.js
, Nuxt.js, and Nest.js are powerful JavaScript frameworks, each with unique strengths and use cases.

Despite their similar names, next.js, nest.js, and nuxt.js are distinct JS frameworks. Let’s see these JS frameworks in detail with their features, benefits, and use cases, and understand the differences without going too technical.
What is next.js?
Next.js is a
React-based framework

used to create server-rendered or statistically generated applications. In server-rendered applications, next.js generates the page content on the server for each user request, ensuring fresh content loads faster. This is particularly useful for commerce websites displaying real-time inventory or business dashboards showing up-to-date data.
For statistically generated applications, next.js serves pre-built pages quickly every time a user visits, improving load times during the development stage.
Key Features of next.js
Built-in APIs

: Next.js ensures the creation of back-end functionalities within the next.js application. In this way, the development process gets simplified, ensuring smoother operations of features like user authentication and data handling.
Quick image loading
: The framework includes built-in tools that automatically optimize images, enhancing the user experience.
Easy styling
: Your website and application will look modern and professional with minimal effort as next.js supports advanced styling techniques.
Smart performance
: Only the intended necessary parts of your web app will load at a time, ensuring maximum performance and elimination of over-resource usage.
Faster updates
: The changes made during the development stage will be updated faster, increasing the pace of deployment.
These features help create a faster, more efficient, and visually appealing website, enhancing user experience and ensuring a top-notch digital presence.
Use Cases:
E-commerce websites:
Ideal for creating dynamic and SEO-friendly online stores.
Content-rich websites:
Perfect for blogs, news sites, and other content-heavy platforms.
Marketing websites:
Great for building fast, SEO-optimized landing pages and promotional sites.
Benefits:
SEO friendly:
Enhanced search engine optimization through server-side rendering and static site generation.
Fast performance:
Efficient rendering techniques and image optimization ensure quick load times.
Versatile and flexible:
Suitable for a wide range of applications, offering flexibility in development and deployment.
What is Nuxt.js?

Nuxt.js is an open-source framework built on Vue.js to easily develop high-end full-stack web applications and websites. These web apps can be rendered on server and client, ensuring better performance and user experience.
Although Nuxt.js and Next.js are built on different underlying libraries (Vue.js for Nuxt.js and React for Next.js), they share similar key features as the frameworks enhance web development.
Key features of Nuxt.js
Universal rendering:
Ensures web pages load quickly and are optimized for search engines, making your site more visible and accessible.
Easy module integration:
Offers various pre-built modules to quickly add features like authentication, analytics, and content management, reducing development time and costs.
State management:
Keeps your app’s data consistent and organized, enhancing reliability and performance.
Optimized loading:
Loads only the necessary parts of your site initially, improving speed and user experience.
Use Cases:
Personal websites:
Ideal for blogs and portfolios, showcasing articles and projects effectively.
Promotional sites:
Perfect for marketing and landing pages that require visitor engagement and fast-loading.
Interactive web apps:
Suitable for progressive web apps (PWAs) that offer a native app-like experience in a web browser.
Benefits:
Efficient development:
Streamlines the development process, leading to quicker project completion and cost savings.
Customizable:
Easily adapts to meet specific business needs, providing a tailored solution.
Strong support:
Backed by a robust community and extensive resources, ensuring continuous improvement and reliable support.
Choosing Nuxt.js ensures that your web application is fast, efficient, and provides an excellent user experience, helping your business stand out in a competitive online landscape.
What is Nest.js?
Nest.js is a Node.js framework used for building efficient, scalable, and reliable server-side applications.

Angular inspires its modular and component-based architecture, and it makes use of TypeScript and JavaScript for app development. This method is perfect for enterprise-level applications and extensive backend systems as it guarantees a well-maintained and organized codebase.
Key Features:
Scalable architecture:
Designed to handle the growth of your application, ensuring it can manage increased traffic and data seamlessly.
Modular structure:
Allows for better organization and reuse of code, making development and maintenance easier and more efficient.
TypeScript support:
Uses TypeScript by default, providing a more robust and error-free coding environment.
Microservices-friendly:
Facilitates the building of microservices, enabling your application to be broken into smaller, manageable pieces that can be developed, deployed, and scaled independently.
Use Cases:
Enterprise-level backends:
Ideal for large-scale applications that require complex backend systems.
Real-time applications:
Perfect for apps that need to process and respond to data in real time, such as chat applications or live data feeds.
API development:
Excellent for creating robust and scalable APIs that serve as the backbone for various client-side applications.
Benefits:
High performance:
Ensures your application runs smoothly even under heavy loads, providing a reliable user experience.
Improved developer productivity:
The modular and TypeScript-based structure reduces development time and minimizes errors.
Future-proof:
Built with scalability and maintainability in mind, ensuring your application can grow and evolve with your business needs.
By choosing Nest.js, you can develop a robust, scalable backend for your application, ensuring it performs well under any conditions and supports your business’s growth and evolving needs.
Next.js vs Nuxt.js vs Nest.js: Comparative analysis

It is essential to comprehend the advantages and areas of expertise of each framework when choosing the appropriate technology for your project. Next.js, Nuxt.js, and Nest.js offer special capabilities and advantages suited to certain areas of web development.

The table below outlines the main differences between these three effective frameworks to understand the differences, whether you’re a business executive overseeing the digital strategy or a decision-maker making sure your technology partners have chosen the right framework.

Analyze the comparison carefully to determine which framework best aligns with your business needs and technical requirements, knowing that your technology partners will choose the optimal solution from these options.
Feature — Next.js — Nuxt.js — Nest.js

Purpose — React-based framework for building web applications with SSR, SSG, and ISR — Vue.js-based framework for building universal and static web applications — TypeScript-based Node.js framework for building scalable server-side applications
Focus — Frontend development with React — Frontend development with Vue.js — Backend development with Node.js
Rendering — SSR, SSG, ISR — SSR, SSG, SPA — Not applicable (backend)
Architecture — Component-based (React) — Component-based (Vue.js) — Modular, TypeScript-based
Language — JavaScript/TypeScript — JavaScript/TypeScript — TypeScript
Community — Large, active community — Large, active community — Growing community
Learning Curve — Moderate (requires React knowledge) — Moderate (requires Vue.js knowledge) — Moderate (requires TypeScript and Node.js knowledge)

Use Cases — Static and dynamic websites, e-commerce, marketing landing pages, blogs — Static and dynamic websites, single-page applications, content-driven websites — RESTful APIs, GraphQL APIs, microservices, server-side logic

Key Features — Image optimization, API routes, data fetching, hybrid static/server rendering — Automatic code splitting, plugin system, content management integration, server-side rendering — Dependency injection, modular architecture, GraphQL support, CLI
Selecting the appropriate JS framework is crucial.

In summary, all these technologies bring unique strengths to your web development. Next.js and Nuxt.js excel at creating fast, SEO-friendly front-end applications with server-side rendering and static site generation, making them ideal for dynamic websites,
e-commerce platforms
, and content-rich sites. Nest.js is best known for building robust, scalable backend systems, perfect for enterprise-level applications and real-time data processing.

For projects requiring a dynamic, SEO-optimized front-end, Next.js or Nuxt.js are excellent choices. For projects that need a strong, scalable backend, Nest.js is the perfect choice. Leveraging the distinct capabilities of each framework can help fulfill the specific needs of a project.

for your project is the best way to initiate it. The right partner will have the skill and experience to understand your requirements and come up with an efficient, reliable, and scalable solution.

title: Diversification & Convergence: What might be the best strategy to meet the digitalization demands?
excerpt: Explore the article to learn about diversification and convergence strategies and how organizations adapt one of them to achieve their digital transformation goals.
author: PM Admin

children.text: The normal way of performing things has changed. Think about going to the movies – you can book tickets from your home now. Think about listening to music – you pay money to avoid ads. Booking flights, and service appointments – everything has become dynamic and can be done from the comfort of your home.
From a neutral standpoint, organizations and technology providers have come a long way. These changes have spurred new strategies that can help businesses to grow.
Diversification and convergence are the two strategies organizations can focus on.
Diversification
focuses on the expansion of a business by investing in multiple areas, industries, or products. This creates a mix of offerings and helps minimize risk while maximizing the chance of growth.
Convergence
refers to the tendency of different systems or technologies to evolve towards performing similar tasks or integrating into a single, multifunctional system.
This article will explore these two strategies and how organizations adapt one of these strategies to achieve their digital transformation goals.
New era, the same process but accomplished by going digital

Digitalization has helped us in many ways. Even on busy days, technology helps us find time for family and wellness. Go back to the time when the banks were crowded with customers coming in and off to make transactions, opening accounts, and more. These facilities became easier and quicker by unifying technology and the process.
We can now literally do banking from home or anywhere. The control is in our hands and with maximum security, we can ensure safe banking.
Let’s consider another example to understand the concept of diversification and convergence strategy.

Imagine a healthcare organization entering the insurance industry. The chances of success are huge as they have the information and the right strategy to provide people with more personalized plans. This convergence would benefit both sides in providing and finding the best insurance coverage plan.
Convergence refers to the tendency of different technologies or systems to evolve towards performing similar tasks or integrating into a single, multifunctional system.

On the other hand, divergence allows an organization or brand to enter into another industry with growth potential. Instead of just focusing on the prominent industry, they find their they find opportunities to use their products or services in another industry.

Apple Inc. is a good example of diversification. They started with iPhones and Mac computers but later they became competitive in Apple Music and Apple TV+. The company spread its investment across two new platforms that entertain people. Over time, they gradually built their reputation and impressed the crowd.

Amazon has followed a similar diversification strategy. They started by selling books online, later becoming the biggest online shopping giant. They have also recognized opportunities in a cloud platform – AWS, a scalable cloud web hosting platform, and Kindle, an electronic device focusing on e-readers. Thus, diversification allows companies to offer a range of products across different industry segments or expand into new markets, reducing their dependence on a single source of revenue.
What strategy is right for my business?
Diversification and convergence strategies are well-known in the business world. However,
adapting a strategy for digital transformation
requires proper analysis before finalizing the best fit. So, to answer the question of what strategy suits my business, it’s essential to consider several factors.
These factors play a pivotal role in developing a successful digital transformation strategy. Let’s see these factors and see how they influence decision-making.
Factors of consideration
Market conditions
Demand Trends
: Analyze the demand for new products or services or identify opportunities to converge the existing systems to better meet customer demands.
Competition
: Understand the market competition and the potential to decide whether to diversify into other areas or converge and strengthen the current position.
Company Resources
Financial Resources
: Evaluate the company’s financial situation to determine the ability to invest in something new opportunities or streamline operations through convergence.
Technical Expertise

: Assess the expertise available within the company or through technology partners. This will help decide whether to leverage the existing knowledge to explore new areas or create synergies through convergence.
Risk Management
Risk Tolerance
: Understand the risk level acceptance rate and plan to spread it or focus on what’s available now.
Business Sustainability
: Consider the business lifecycle and experience of the company, the more years it sustains, the more it leans towards diversification, while a growing company converges to consolidate gains.
Innovation to Future
Technological Advancements
: Consider technological trends to see if they favor diversification into new tech areas or the convergence of technologies to create new solutions.
Disruption Potential
: Evaluate the potential for industry disruption and decide if diversification can provide a hedge against it or if convergence can create an offering itself.
Customer Intention
Customer Segmentation
: Learn the customer segments and their desire to determine if they love to see a brand in multiple areas or if they upgrade the existing products/services for reinforcement.
Customer Feedback
: Make use of feedback to choose a strategy, meeting their direct demands.

In addition to these considerations, companies must also comply with regulations and legal norms. This is especially important if the technology fundamentally changes how customers interact with your business. When a new initiative becomes popular and widely adopted, regulatory questions often arise. Whether you’re diversifying or converging, your operations must adhere to established rules.
How organizations can implement diversification and convergence strategies?
For organizations and brands pursuing digital transformation, the concepts of diversification and convergence have significant implications:

A diversification strategy in digital transformation involves expanding the range of services or products an organization offers. Consider a solar panel manufacturer who decides to expand their product line to include smart solar panels with IoT sensors following digital transformation. The company also plans to provide mobile applications for customers and field service agents.

In this case, digital transformation based on a diversification strategy would be ideal. This new expansion strategy, planned by considering all the factors, aims to improve customer experience and streamline field service management.

By diversifying into digital services, the manufacturer can attract new customers, offer more value to the existing customer base, and establish a stronger presence in the smart energy market. Diversification can thus support these companies to invest in new markets and customer segments, driving growth and innovation.
On the other hand, the
convergence strategy
for digital transformation focuses on the integration of technology stack and processes to develop more cohesive and efficient systems.

For instance, a company providing identification products or user interface solutions could leverage a convergence strategy to develop more solutions-focused products customized to manufacturing requirements. Integrating various digital tools could their commitment to customers and their technical knowledge in handling custom projects. This can help the company evolve into an expertise solutions provider, generating new leads, improved customer experiences, and increased operational efficiency.
In essence, for companies seeking digital transformation:
Diversification
is about
expanding
their digital capabilities and offerings to explore new opportunities and markets.
Convergence
is about
integrating
digital processes and technologies to enhance efficiency and create a seamless experience for both employees and customers.

Both strategies are crucial for staying competitive in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. Companies with a balance in diversification with convergence can expect to see improved performance, greater customer satisfaction, and a stronger position in the digital economy. A digital transformation partner can help you acknowledge all these factors and find a strategy based on the business needs.
A
digital transformation company
can achieve
diversification
by continuously innovating and incorporating emerging technologies into its portfolio and addressing a broader range of customer needs. To realize
convergence
, the company can focus on integrating its various digital services and platforms to provide a seamless and efficient user experience across all touchpoints.

title: E-commerce Ultimate Guide to Launching and Growing Your Digital Business
excerpt: Explore everything you need to know to launch your e-commerce business with a solid strategy and actionable plan.
author: PM Admin

children.text: E-commerce continues to grow as more people choose online channels for convenient shopping. Statistics reinforce this trend, with global online sales expected to reach 7.9 trillion dollars. Where does that position your brand? If you’re missing out on potential online buyers, it’s worth considering e-commerce as part of your business strategy.

Moving from traditional operations to a digital platform is a significant step. Whether you’re exploring online sales for the first time or aiming to grow your digital presence, there’s much to consider—from crafting the right strategy to selecting features that enhance the customer experience.
This guide covers everything you need to know to launch your e-commerce business with a solid strategy and actionable plan.
Types of e-commerce and which definition fits your business

Selling products between businesses and selling directly to customers are two different processes. The first scenario, where two businesses are involved, is called Business-to-Business (B2B). In contrast, selling products directly to customers is called Business-to-Consumer (B2C).

Similarly, two more models are becoming prominent in the e-commerce terminology: Customer-to-Customer (C2C) and Direct-to-Customer (D2C). What makes them different from the traditional B2B and B2C e-commerce models?

Consider this: you have a few electronic items you no longer want, and you decide to sell them. You set up an ad for your used items on platforms like eBay, and someone buys them. This is a C2C model, where one customer sells to another, often involving pre-owned goods. The original idea behind C2C was to create platforms where individuals could trade directly with each other without formal businesses being involved. Other examples include:
An individual renting out their spare room on Airbnb
Someone offering handmade crafts on Etsy
In some sources, C2C may also be called
Peer-to-Peer (P2P)
or
Individual-to-Individual (I2I)
, but the concept remains the same, regardless of the terminology.

D2C, on the other hand, is similar to B2B, where businesses sell their products directly to the consumer, cutting out third-party wholesalers, retailers, and distributors. D2C allows brands to have complete control over the customer journey, offering deeper insights into consumer behavior. This model works especially well for businesses with high-demand products that are exclusively available through their brand’s store, whether physical or online. However, sales can fluctuate based on market demand and trends.
Here is a quick overview of these definitions.
B2B (Business-to-Business): Transactions between two businesses.
B2C (Business-to-Consumer): Businesses selling products or services directly to individual consumers.
C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer): Platforms that facilitate transactions between individual consumers.
D2C (Direct-to-Consumer): Manufacturers or brands selling directly to end consumers, bypassing traditional retail channels.
Key pillars of a successful e-commerce strategy: A holistic approach
The primary step for developing an
e-commerce platform

that matches your business requirements is to have a good understanding of what or how you want to sell your products. Being unique will always make a business stand out in the crowd. The uniqueness may refer to the products you sell, how they are projected to consumers, or the marketing strategy.

A successful e-commerce strategy helps to address all these key components and consider them before implementation. Let’s explore the essential pillars that form the foundation of a robust e-commerce strategy:
1. Customer-centric approach
In the world of endless choices, customer experience is your differentiator. Focus on:
Personalization across all touchpoints
Omnichannel customer support
Loyalty programs that truly add value
Remember, acquiring a customer is just the beginning – retaining them is where the magic happens.
2. Streamlined operations
Behind every successful e-commerce business is a well-oiled machine. Prioritize:

title: What Is Preventive Maintenance? Everything One Needs To Know
excerpt: Preventive Maintenance is routine maintenance performed on a fixed schedule to minimize the chance of unplanned breakdowns and increase asset life.
author: PM Admin

children.text: With preventive maintenance, this costly mistake could have been prevented in the early stages!
A
furniture manufacturing company

faced frequent equipment failures, leading to downtime. Though the company had a maintenance team, the strategy wasn’t ideal and faced acute challenges. Analyzing the situation, the company identified the weakness in the maintenance department, particularly in preventive maintenance practices.

Sometimes, reactive maintenance is not the right strategy; hence, as a solution, the company planned to enhance the efficiency of its preventive maintenance. The result was as expected; the company minimized equipment failures and downtime, improving operational efficiency and reducing maintenance costs.
These situations highlight the importance of preventive maintenance in industrial or manufacturing operations.
What is Preventive Maintenance?

Preventive Maintenance is routine maintenance performed on a fixed schedule to minimize the chance of unplanned breakdowns and increase asset life. Instead of waiting for failure (reactive maintenance), businesses maintain equipment based on time, usage, or condition-based triggers on a schedule.

For example, regularly applying oil to large machines for lubrication is essential. No one waits until a machine begins to seize before taking action; instead, lubrication is done on time to ensure smooth operation. This is a routine task in a typical preventive maintenance schedule.
It is required for businesses to:
Overcome unexpected breakdowns and minimize operating costs
Maximizes asset life, delays costly replacements
Reduces maintenance costs by fixing minor issues before they grow
Makes the process and operations run smoothly
Ensures the business complies with the standards of regulation
Prevention saves businesses, time, and money by not letting things break in the first place before they fail.
The Business Impact of Preventive Maintenance
For different stakeholders in an organization, the impact of Preventive Maintenance varies.
For CEOs & Business Owners:
Boosts profitability by minimizing costly downtime.
Enhances brand reputation by ensuring consistent product/service delivery.
Optimizes asset ROI, delaying capital expenditures on new equipment.
For Maintenance Managers:
Improves efficiency by reducing emergency repairs.
Enables better planning with scheduled maintenance and resource allocation.
Reduces stress; fewer emergency jobs.
For Technicians & Frontline Workers:
Safer working conditions with fewer equipment malfunctions.
Less pressure—working proactively instead of firefighting issues.
Clearer workflows with structured maintenance schedules.
Preventive Maintenance isn’t just about fixing things—it’s about running a smarter, more profitable business.
Preventive Maintenance vs. Other Strategies: What’s the Difference?

There are a few more strategies to ensure higher uptime of a device. While each strategy is relevant to businesses, there are definite stages of adapting them. While the primary concept is reactive, where maintenance efforts are more aligned to repair after an event of issue has already happened. Whereas, the latter ensures avoiding them but differentiates based on the affordability of a company.
Strategy — Approach — Pros — Cons
Reactive Maintenance — Fixing equipment only after it breaks — Low initial cost, easy to implement — High downtime, expensive emergency repairs
Preventive Maintenance — Scheduled maintenance to prevent failures — Reduces downtime, extends asset life — Requires upfront planning and resource allocation
Predictive Maintenance — Uses real-time data to predict failures — Optimizes maintenance schedules, minimizes breakdowns — Higher cost due to advanced monitoring technology
Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) — Company-wide proactive maintenance culture — Improves overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) — Requires extensive workforce involvement and training
Preventive Maintenance is a balanced approach, offering a structured yet cost-effective way to ensure operational reliability.
Overcoming Challenges of Deploying Preventive Maintenance and How to Overcome Them?

Like any strategy, preventive maintenance is susceptible to challenges. However, they are not a concern if properly planned and executed. The strategy must be like – expand as you go, rather than starting big. Analyzing the effectiveness and the insights from the results reassures investing in it as things start moving forward.
High Initial Costs
Start small – begin working on key assets and progressively implement it.
No Skilled workforce
Train your technicians in predictive/preventive maintenance techniques.
Change Management
Let stakeholders know long-term investment costs and efficiency benefits.
Data Issues
CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management Systems) is used to track data on a more systematic level.
Begin Preventive Maintenance In Your Business
Now that we know about the challenges and their solutions, it’s time to make the first steps.
Step 1
: Identify Critical Assets
Start by focusing on the machinery that is critical to business operations and has higher downtime costs.
Step 2
: Formulate a Maintenance Plan
When in doubt, manufacturer recommendations and usage data lead the way followed by know-how and history from past failures.
Step 3
: Use CMMS
An online tracking system is used to schedule and track maintenance activities better.
Step 4
: Train your team
Ensure that preventive tasks are prioritized and understood by all, including maintenance staff and laborers.
Step 5
: Remain vigilant and make it a process of continual enhancement
Leverage maintenance KPIs like MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) and Mean Time to Repair as your map progresses.
Preparing a Checklist for Planned Maintenance

This ensures uniform and swift maintenance practices through a well-rounded checklist. Checklist varies per industry and its components, but for a start, here is an example of a preventive maintenance checklist for a manufacturing machine:
Lubricate moving parts weekly
Inspect and replace worn-out belts quarterly
Test safety systems monthly
Clean filters and vents every two weeks
Check for unusual vibrations or noises daily
Form customized checklists according to industry practices and equipment types.
Takeaway

Preventive maintenance keeps machines running and creates an attractive culture of reliability, process efficiency, and cost savings. Downtime costs from maintenance are offset, and the business that proactively manages its assets goes one step ahead to stay profitable in the long term for competitive advantage.
A well-planned strategy that identifies machinery requiring regular maintenance, combined with a
preventive maintenance CMMS software

, can help businesses achieve the rare goal of maximizing uptime. These software solutions automate PM tasks, manage assets, schedule jobs, and assign maintenance teams to ensure an efficient and effective maintenance process. To implement the best strategy, connect with experts from PM software providers, share your asset data, and collaborate to develop a tailored maintenance plan that works for your operations.

title: Laravel – The most popular PHP framework | A definitive guide
excerpt: Explore the comprehensive guide to learn all about Laravel, one of the promising and popular PHP framework.
author: PM Admin

children.text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.
~ Kent Beck

As Kent Beck wisely stated, transforming concepts into reality requires a balance of functionality, accuracy, and efficiency. Developers face the formidable challenge of navigating this balance and having an optimal framework that minimizes the learning curve while delivering swift results is essential.
Globally, over 80 million websites use PHP as their programming language. Developers, in turn, leverage frameworks as foundational platforms to develop web applications, with
Laravel
standing out as the most popular and supported framework within a thriving community.
Let’s explore the comprehensive guide and understand a good deal about the Laravel framework.
What is Laravel?
Laravel is a PHP framework characterized by a graceful coding style and braced by extensive community support. The framework adheres to an easy-to-follow
development process
Quick facts about Laravel
A platform for constructing PHP web applications
Boasts a vast code library
Facilitates faster development times
Ideal for creating secure and scalable web applications
A glance at the usage statistics in comparison to other PHP frameworks will underscore the widespread acceptance of this model.
Data courtesy: BuiltWith

CodeIgniter is another framework that falls into a similarly popular category. Therefore, we have selected it for comparison alongside three other frameworks for analysis: CakePHP, Symfony, and Yii. The number of websites developed using Laravel is an impressive 1,601,267!
Why is Laravel so popular and best for web development?

The intention behind creating Laravel, developed by Taylor Otwell, was simple: to assist developers in simplifying their work. In short, it aims to offer simple, faster, and better development solutions.

The primary reason for its popularity lies in delivering precisely what it is intended to provide — peace of mind! Here are nine other reasons that make Laravel the optimal choice for web development.
1. The transformation phase
Swift deployment to market
A modular platform
Abundance of pre-built functionalities and structures
Time-efficient solution
Elimination of the need to write individual lines of code
2. Built-in user authentication & authorization support
With Laravel, creating a web application or website with user authentication and authorization is straightforward. For instance, applications featuring user account functionalities for
Field Service Management Solutions
, such as the following:
Login,
Register,
and Password reset
can be effortlessly implemented with a single command! Organizing these functionalities is uncomplicated as they are readily available as built-in features.
3. Secure from malicious attacks & safety vulnerabilities

Some days, while browsing the internet, we may encounter websites displaying messages such as “Error 500 – Internal Error” or “Error 503 – Service Unavailable.” What are these errors, and why do they occur? The web security team often identifies these issues as potential attacks.

Web attacks have become a persistent concern in the digital world. A previously well-functioning application can suddenly crash due to security vulnerabilities. Fortunately, the security fixes logs in Laravel offer a promising solution. The platform provides security measures against:
SQL injection
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks
Cross-site scripting
4. Well-defined MVC structure

The MVC structure adopted by the Laravel framework is considered among the best, featuring a well-defined architectural pattern. Moreover, developers can modify the structure while keeping the base unchanged. This structure brings several advantages, including:
Improved documentation
Enhanced performance
Availability of numerous built-in functionalities
Take a closer look at the MVC structure of Laravel, and appreciate the organized nature of its architecture.
5. Testing support
The framework offers outstanding support for
automation QA testing, providing expressive testing capabilities
for applications developed on this platform.

Notably, one of its highly regarded features is its unit testing capability, allowing testing of each component or module of the application. This makes it an ideal choice for developing high-performance and optimized web code.
6. Automatic command schedule

Suppose you have an application that necessitates sending email reminders or notifications. Traditionally, developers had to run a cron job for each task to schedule email notifications. However, with Laravel, this process has evolved.

In the Laravel framework, developers can define the command schedule within the framework itself. A single cron entry on the server is all it takes to execute this task, streamlining the process and making it more efficient.
7. Message queue system for load balancing

What if your online customer base experiences a sudden surge, say by 2x? In these scenarios, the application requires proper load balancing to accommodate the increased traffic. Failure to do so would result in escalated hosting efforts.

The Laravel framework is designed with scalability, allowing developers to optimize applications seamlessly in response to varying traffic. This ensures efficient server maintenance and effective traffic management.

The key component enabling this scalability is the message queue system. The queue service in Laravel provides a unified API across various queue back-ends, facilitating smooth and robust handling of tasks and messages.
8. Mail integration compatibility
Email is a powerful conversation starter for client prospecting, and nearly every web platform leverages email integration to achieve this goal or pursue other strategic objectives.

Laravel, in particular, is equipped with the SwiftMailer library, offering a clean and straightforward API configuration for individual email accounts. This feature enhances the platform’s capability to seamlessly integrate email functionalities into web applications, contributing to effective communication and client engagement.
9. Loading…, the least!

Laravel has a built-in file configuration that facilitates loading URLs within the framework, defining accessible and identifiable routes. The key functionality enabling this lightweight loading capability in web applications is URL routing.

URL routing empowers developers to configure applications to accept request URLs that may not necessarily map to physical files. Instead, it allows web content to display within the current sub-page without redirection to other links.
Now that we comprehend the reasons behind Laravel’s popularity, let’s delve into its specific advantages.
Advantages of Laravel framework
Easy to get started and implement
Simple to follow the syntax, especially for newbies
Vast built-in library
Easy deployment to major cloud service providers
Powerful Blade templating engine
Secure, robust, and scalable
However, every coin has two sides, and it’s essential to understand the potential drawbacks. Let’s explore the disadvantages of Laravel.
Disadvantages of Laravel Framework
Slower compared to other frameworks due to the vast built-in library
Developers need to exercise caution during version upgrades due to potential compatibility issues
Do not inherently support payment services but provides a library for integrating payment modules
Not ideal for mobile applications
Let’s look into the features of the framework.
6 important Laravel features you may find instrumental
1. Blade template engine

What is the Blade Template Engine in Laravel? It’s an engine that empowers developers to construct HTML-based designs and themes. Leveraging the Blade concept, developers can create straightforward layouts. Blade offers numerous advantages, such as:
Adds zero overhead to web applications
No restrictions in using plain PHP code in views
A lightweight template
Many widgets are available to incorporate with CSS and JS codes
2. Eloquent ORM

What is Eloquent ORM in Laravel? Eloquent is an Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) that comes included by default within the Laravel framework. Essentially, it’s software that facilitates seamless interaction with the database through a straightforward ActiveRecord implementation.

Eloquent allows developers to write database queries using PHP syntax, eliminating them from knowing or writing SQL for database modification. This simplifies the process and serves as a significant time-saving mechanism.
3. Vast library & MVC structure
As mentioned earlier, Laravel holds a significant advantage over other frameworks due to its extensive object-oriented library. This pre-installed library greatly simplifies development efforts.

The MVC (Model, View, and Controller) structure ensures robust separation between the presentation layer and business logic. Essentially, it’s a design pattern that segregates the model (logic and data handling), the view (UI), and the controller process (interface). This separation enhances code organization, maintainability, and overall application structure.
4. Open-source platform

With the support of a vast community, validating the features of the Laravel platform becomes straightforward. The framework includes a ValidationRequest by default, a trait controlling HTTP requests. This trait automatically checks errors in session data and generates views, streamlining the validation process and enhancing the overall robustness of the application.
5. Migration system

What is the migration system in Laravel? It is a feature that empowers developers to create tables in the database. This functionality utilizes PHP to write a migration statement for database creation instead of SQL.
In Laravel, the principle “what works with PHP stays active” emphasizes the seamless integration and alignment with the PHP programming language throughout the framework.
6. Localization

One of the outstanding features that contributes to the global acceptance of the framework is localization. The Laravel platform enables the creation of multilingual applications, using multilingual string functions.

Developers can access strings in various languages seamlessly by employing the trans() helper, providing a convenient and efficient way to manage and implement multilingual capabilities in their applications.
Bonus content
Laravel for multi-purpose project requirements
Explore the packages available in the Laravel framework for numerous project requirements. Laravel is the best for various project requirements.
Web application with subscriptions – Cashier
Zero downtime PHP deployment – Envoyer
Channel subscription & podcasts – Laravel echo
Task automation & migration – Artisan
A quick comparison with other frameworks
Laravel works for all; the reason for this statement is due to the limitations that exist in other frameworks. You can find the curbs of the three PHP frameworks compared to Laravel.
Yii
– Struggles with poorly drafted Ajax features and a dependency on static methods.
CodeIgniter
– Not deemed suitable for large-scale projects.
Symfony
– Challenges with file parsing complexities – not the best choice for small-scale projects.
Laravel combinations

Laravel follows the MVC architecture, signifying that the framework is versatile enough to be employed in developing comprehensive applications encompassing both the back-end and front-end. Opting for Laravel to create a full-stack web application is a common choice among developers.
A few combinations work exceptionally well with Laravel. Here are the two most suitable combinations of Laravel.
Laravel + Vue.js
The combination of Laravel and
Vue.js

yields numerous advantages. Vue.js enhances user experience by providing a richer and more engaging interface, establishing seamless connectivity. The application becomes powerful when integrated with Laravel, the premier back-end PHP framework, and Vue.js, a prominent front-end JavaScript framework.

Vue.js facilitates the creation of a front end that updates without requiring page reloads each time the application changes. This is achieved through the virtual DOM, which efficiently responds to page updates, maintaining stable web performance. Furthermore, the learning curve for implementation is minimal, contributing to a smoother development process.
Laravel + React
React

and Laravel forms one of the best combinations to deliver a magnificent user experience. React, a JavaScript framework excels in building independent single-page applications (SPAs), mobile or hybrid apps, and even television applications.
Together, this combination offers several benefits, including:
Quick page loading
Easy maintenance
Bandwidth savings by avoiding the need to write HTML codes for all pages
Moreover, this combination is an excellent choice for constructing SEO-friendly websites.
Laravel + Angular
With
Angular

, a front-end JavaScript framework, page loading eases progress tracking. The performance of web applications increases when combined with the Laravel framework. How does the performance increase with this combination?

The reason is the way the page loads; there is no need to load the entire page, just the parts needed for loading. Also, the applications become more responsive. For example, when a customer form is implemented, it validates quickly for developer feedback.

Laravel, with any of the three front-end choices, can lead to the development of exceptional applications. Laravel developers can choose the front-end framework based on project requirements, making decision-making easier with experience.
Top websites running using the Laravel framework
Disney
New York Times
Warner Bros
Invoice Ninja
Alison
Laracasts
Final thoughts

Concluding the article, the provided data underscores the evident utility and popularity of Laravel as a PHP framework. Laravel stands out as a versatile and reliable choice for developers. It facilitates the creation of compelling websites and applications, ensuring speed and robust security. The framework’s adaptability makes it suitable for a wide range of business projects; spanning from small-scale to large-scale endeavors.

Based on the research data, one undeniable fact emerges: Laravel empowers developers to craft high-quality digital solutions efficiently. Its blend of speed, security, and scalability positions it as a top-tier option in PHP frameworks. This makes it an excellent resource for the developer community, offering a robust foundation for many projects.

excerpt: Learn why brands must consider React Native for creating cross-platform mobile application for their project. A smart way to build the future.
author: PM Admin

children.text: After a minute dip in 2022, post-pandemic season, the market reclaimed its energy bar in 2023, speculating the same trend in 2024 and the following years. Statistics suggest,
as per reports

, that global mobile application downloads have reached 257 billion in 2023. In terms of spending, the average consumer spend on mobile apps from 2021 to 2023 per smartphone was approximately 5.08 U.S.

As the trend suggests, the demand for mobile applications attracts businesses and organizations to invest in the small screen platforms. When it comes to developing a mobile application, starting from scratch requires a proper planning and collaboration with a technical partner. The question is what’s the best technology suitable for your project and the platforms to target?

If you are planning for a lucrative, high-performing mobile application for iOS, Android, or Windows, i.e., multiple platforms, then React Native is the best choice. Here’s why companies and organizations are choosing this trendy technology for their mobile app development projects:
Propel your mobile app development with React Native: 7 compelling benefits

React Native, a JavaScript-based framework emerges as a powerful tool for organizations and companies seeking to accelerate mobile app development while simultaneously achieving superior results. Here are seven compelling benefits of incorporating React Native into your next mobile app endeavor:
Cross-Platform Development:

Achieve optimal reach by eliminating the need for separate codebases for iOS and Android. React Native’s “write once, run anywhere” philosophy translates to faster development, streamlined maintenance, and reduced resource allocation.
Native Performance and Feel:

Leverage the framework’s utilization of native UI components and APIs to deliver exceptional performance and an authentic user experience indistinguishable from truly native apps—no compromises on quality or responsiveness.
Cost-Effectiveness:

The shared codebase of React Native significantly reduces development time and associated costs. Moreover, the large JavaScript developer community allows for potentially lower talent acquisition costs compared to specialized native developers.
Accelerated Time to Market:
By eliminating the duplication of development efforts, React Native empowers you to launch your app faster, capitalize on market opportunities sooner, and gain a competitive edge.
Continuous Innovation:

Backed by Facebook and a thriving developer community, React Native benefits from frequent updates, performance enhancements, and the integration of cutting-edge technologies, ensuring your app remains future-proof.
Simplified Maintenance:

Managing a single codebase reduces the overhead and complexity associated with maintaining separate native apps. Updates and bug fixes can be implemented effortlessly across both platforms simultaneously.
Integration with Existing Web Dev Teams:

If you possess a team skilled in JavaScript web development, leveraging React Native opens a seamless transition into mobile app development, maximizing team expertise and minimizing training requirements.
React Native vs. other cross-platform frameworks: Navigating the choices

While React Native shines as a popular option, you may be required to know some of the other cross-platform frameworks. Let’s explore some of these frameworks and their strengths for a quick comparison.
React Native:
Leverages JavaScript:
Familiar for web developers, reducing onboarding time and potentially lowering costs.
Native Performance:
Utilizes native UI components for a smooth and responsive experience.
Active Community and Development:
Backed by Facebook and a vibrant community, ensuring constant updates and resources.
Third-Party Ecosystem:
A rich library of pre-built components and functionalities accelerates development.
Flutter:
Hot Reloading:
Enables instant code updates, boosting development speed and iteration.
Custom UI Toolkit:
Offers more control over UI customization for unique app designs.
Strong Performance:
Generally considered to deliver native-like performance on both iOS and Android.
Learning Curve:
Requires familiarity with Dart, potentially requiring additional learning for developers.
Xamarin:
Direct Native Access:
Provides unparalleled access to native features and functionalities for complete control.
Mature and Stable:
Backed by Microsoft, offering a robust and well-established platform.
Native-Like Performance:
Delivers top-notch performance due to its utilization of native languages (C# and Kotlin).
Development Cost:
Requires developers proficient in both C# and Kotlin, potentially increasing costs.
Ionic:
Fastest Development:
Leverages web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for rapid development.
Largest Community:
Boasts a massive community and abundant resources for easy troubleshooting and learning.
Cost-Effective:
Relatively lower development costs due to its ease of use and readily available resources.
Performance Limitations:
Can struggle to achieve native-like performance, especially for complex apps.

The optimal framework hinges on the specific project needs, budget, and team expertise. An experienced technology partner will consider various factors like requirement complexity, time-to-market pace, and scalability to choose the best technology suitable for the project needs.
The future of React Native: Mobile & beyond
While React Native has solidified its position as a leading framework for
cross-platform mobile development
, its potential extends far beyond smartphones and tablets. The future of React Native is bright, as its reach expands to encompass diverse platforms and unlock exciting new possibilities.
Native Desktop Apps:
While primarily focused on mobile, React Native frameworks for
Windows

React | A future-proof & dynamic JavaScript framework

React is a JavaScript library utilized for creating interactive and dynamic user interfaces, especially well-suited for single-page applications where user interactions necessitate frequent updates of the displayed content. This library empowers developers to construct modular UI components that are both reusable and can be seamlessly composed to craft intricate user interfaces, enhancing efficiency in the development process. The forthcoming sections of this blog will delve into the various applications of React.

This technology has empowered developers to construct dynamic web applications swiftly, resulting in faster development cycles and simplified maintenance. React plays a pivotal role in rendering views for both web and mobile applications, earning widespread adoption, including usage by many popular companies.
Now, let’s explore two key factors defining this framework’s essence.
Component-Based Architecture

: React enables developers to create reusable components independent of each other. Therefore, if a critical feature of a web application breaks, the remaining elements continue to function. The Virtual DOM facilitates updating components when a user interacts without affecting other parts of the interface. You will discover more about Virtual DOM in the next few minutes.
Unidirectional Data Flow

: The data flow starts with a single source known as the state, which holds the current data and represents the application’s current state. This data is passed down to different components in a hierarchical structure, each receiving the data it needs from its parent component. It can also pass down the data to its child components.

However, the flow of data always moves in one direction, from parent to child, and never in the opposite way. Unidirectional data flow simplifies the understanding of how data changes and updates occur within the application, contributing to maintaining the codebase perfectly.
Benefits React brings to a project for an organization or business.

provides solutions for many complex issues faced by businesses and organizations.
Take a look at the advantages of including React in a technology stack for businesses and organizations:
Enhanced Performance

React introduced the Virtual DOM, a lightweight representation of the actual DOM. When changes occur, React updates the Virtual DOM first, then efficiently identifies and applies only the necessary changes to the real DOM. The result – minimizes re-rendering, leading to improved performance and faster user interface updates.
Component Reusability

React promotes a modular, component-based approach to UI development. Developers can create independent and reusable components like buttons, input fields, or complex UI elements. This modularity accelerates development and ensures consistency across the application, reusing the same components in different parts of the project.
Increased Developer Productivity

React’s declarative syntax and use of JavaScript simplify the development process. Developers can focus on describing how the UI should look in different states, and React takes care of efficiently updating the DOM. This simplicity and the use of a single language (JavaScript) enhance developer productivity, allowing for faster development cycles and quicker adaptation to changes.
Scalability

React’s component-based architecture facilitates scalability. As demand increases, developers can easily add new or scale existing components. The modular structure makes it simpler to manage complex applications, enabling businesses to scale their projects without sacrificing performance or maintainability.
Responsive User Interfaces

The Virtual DOM enables React to update only the changed components, minimizing the impact on the overall user interface. This results in a more responsive application, crucial for delivering a seamless and enjoyable user experience, which is particularly important for retaining and engaging users.
Strong Community Support

React has a large and active community of developers worldwide. This community contributes to many resources, tutorials, and third-party libraries. Businesses benefit from this collective knowledge, finding solutions to common challenges, receiving timely support, and staying informed about best practices and updates through technology partners.
Cross-Platform Development

React Native, an extension of React, allows businesses to use the same codebase for web and mobile applications. This streamlines development and reduces the need for separate teams and resources for web and mobile projects. Businesses can maintain a consistent user experience across multiple platforms.
Ecosystem and Tools

React’s ecosystem includes various tools and libraries that complement its core functionality. Businesses can leverage these tools for tasks like state management, routing, and testing, enhancing the overall development process. Technology binds the past, present, and future

The advantages of integrating this technology into your business project are thus immensely beneficial. title: How to find a balance between SEO and creative website design?
excerpt: Mobile-first matters: Striking the right balance between optimized content (SEO) and web design is today's toughest challenge.
author: PM Admin

children.text: Graphic design legend Milton Glaser said, “The purpose of design is to inform and delight.” This is true because a great web design is all about making an impact on the viewer/user. But design alone cannot deliver or attract traffic. Content, when created and integrated seamlessly with the design component, can increase the visibility of your brand, generate traffic, and aid quicker conversions. However, finding the right balance between content, especially optimized content (SEO) and
website design
is the trickiest part.
Read on to learn how to create content and design that complement each other.
Decide on the core objective
In the case of
web development

, this is the most fundamental and crucial question to ask – What do you want to achieve from this website or webpage? Do you wish this to be the landing page for a paid advertising campaign? Then you will benefit by prioritizing a streamlined user experience (UX) over an
advanced SEO strategy
. However, if you want the page to rank organically on search engine results pages (SERPs), you should focus on how to best optimize the content while providing a great UX simultaneously.
Focus on Content – See How Much is Appropriate

Remember you don’t need beautiful pages that lack important information. Similarly, you are better off without SEO-oriented pages with tacky designs as well. Although there isn’t a hard and fast rule to decide how much (content and design) is too much, the rule of thumb is ‘users know it’. Test out a few page designs and see what works best. Does reducing the word count on the page impact the click-through rates? How does it affect your keyword rankings? What happens when you add a little bit more information to the page? If your page is becoming more relevant and sticky and users are staying for longer, you have cracked the secret to a successful SEO-design combo. Experimentation is the only way to achieve on-page optimization.
Choose Fonts, Images and Animations Wisely

Fancy fonts, gaudy layouts, and flashy animations are a surefire recipe for website disaster. Use a minimum number of fonts and ensure they bring about symmetry in the page while also reducing the loading time.  Similarly, following image optimization and merging images helps cut down the loading time and improve the aesthetics of the web page.
Accept that SEO isn’t all About Keywords

SEO indeed relies on using the appropriate keywords. However, it is also important to create content that is engaging and informative. Merely stuffing keywords into your content will not fetch good results, and may even backfire as some of the websites get blacklisted for keyword stuffing. Content experts say, “When you focus your efforts on writing what matters, your keywords will enter the arena naturally.”
Final Word/Conclusion

The need for a balance between SEO and website design is stronger today, more than ever, thanks to the ubiquitous presence of smartphones. Drawing site traffic is as difficult as making the visitor stay on the page/website. Only the perfect blend of design and SEO can help achieve both objectives. The user experience should be at the center of every design and content effort.

Engage graphic designers and content writers to research and develop fresh designs and content for the new look of the site. Website redesign doesn’t have to be a complete makeover, tweaking the existing website to ensure smooth performance and rich user experience is enough.
Once the design and content are ready, get your website developer to implement the changes.

The entire website redesign operation should have your designer, researcher writer, and developer onboard from the very beginning so that there is no lack of communication and the task gets accomplished with zero to minimal disruption.

title: How to set up an eCommerce website for instant conversions
excerpt: The e-commerce store looks attractive with pretty colors and images. Now it’s time to get the customers land on the homepage of your site
author: PM Admin

children.text: The e-commerce store looks attractive with pretty colors and images. Now it’s time to get the customers land on the homepage of your site. When we talk about e-commerce, we must realize that getting the customers attention is not enough as the success of your store depends on the conversion rate.
What is Conversion Rate?
Conversion rate refers to a number of visitors to your website who actually took the action you wanted them to take. For example, buying a product or signing up for the newsletter.

E-commerce entrepreneurs must invest in ways to innovate their websites so as to generate instant and more conversions. According to a survey conducted by the E-marketers, E-commerce is expected to expand to 12.4 percent of the world’s economy by 2019. To achieve successful e-commerce performance and high rate of conversion, customer experience is paramount.
The Importance of Rate of Conversions in E-commerce

Conversion rate optimization is one of the most important metrics which determines the success of an e-commerce website. Every individual decision made in e-commerce impacts the rate at which the visitors convert to purchase.

Conversion rate helps in predicting future success by measuring the business profitability and by determining the shortcomings of the e-commerce website. The average conversion rate for e-commerce is approximately 2-3 percent.
How to increase the Ecommerce Conversion Rates?

Using a proactive approach towards improving the experience of the customers visiting the e-commerce website helps in exceeding customer expectations. By considering the following points while setting up an e-commerce website, the conversion rates may be greatly improved:
Reducing the number of form fields:

The websites must aim at deriving only the necessary information from the customers to value their time and privacy. According to a recent study, forms with three fields are expected to get 25 percent higher conversions as compared to the forms having more than four fields.
Removing automatic image sliders:

Due to the automatic image sliders, the website users tend to lose control which could lead to the user bouncing off the website. According to a study conducted by NNGroup.com, there is a symptom called banner blindness which means there are certain category of users who tend to ignore anything which appears to resemble an advertisement.
Using high quality real and relatable photos:
In order to give a real and authentic appeal to the users, the e-commerce websites must discard stock images and try to use high-quality real images to help them increase their conversion rate.
Use Live Chat to exceed customer satisfaction:

According to research, 77 percent of the users using live chat believe that their queries are attended to quickly and efficiently, 61 percent using email believe their questions are being quickly answered and 44 percent of the users using phone calls were satisfied. Live chat not only helps in bringing the customers closer but also generates traffic from mouth to mouth publicity.
Displaying the company’s phone number on the e-commerce website:
The customers tend to trust the websites which display their contact details and phone numbers and this can greatly help in increasing the conversion rate.
Using the ‘Principle of Scarcity’:

It is the psychology of the customers to assign more value to the products which are available in lesser numbers than the ones which are available in abundance. Displaying an inventory meter for the products on the e-commerce website is a good idea to improve conversions.
Include Site-Search option:

On-Site search tool enables quicker product discovery and thus helps in saving the user’s time. The search data is an important by-product of site search option which further helps in targeting marketing campaigns better by identifying which products are being most searched for by the customers.
Others:

Some of the other features which when included in e-commerce website help in improving the conversion rates include testimonials, recommendations by experts or stylists, descriptive product details, etc.
By including the features mentioned above in an
e-commerce website

, it is most likely the conversions will go up, however, at the same time, it is very crucial to analyze the impact of these features on a timely basis and make modifications that bring a higher number of conversions to the website.
